description: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server — multi-framework model serving (ONNX, TensorRT, PyTorch, Python backend, ensembles). Docker-compose scaffold with a model_repository layout, an identity/echo model for smoke-testing, and a tritonclient HTTP example. For serving classical ML (ResNet, Whisper, embeddings) and mixed ONNX/TensorRT pipelines at NVIDIA-optimized latency.

buildHints.whenToUse: Pick Triton when the workload is classical ML (CV/ASR/embeddings/recommenders), when you're combining ONNX + TensorRT + Python backends in ensembles, or when NVIDIA-specific optimizations (TensorRT, CUDA graphs, dynamic batching) matter. For pure LLM serving use vllm-server / sglang-server / tgi-server — they're faster and simpler for that shape.
firstSteps: Add a model: drop weights under model_repository/<name>/<version>/ (e.g. `model.onnx` or `model.plan`)
Write/edit model_repository/<name>/config.pbtxt — platform, inputs, outputs, dynamic_batching
docker compose up -d (pulls ~15GB — tritonserver image is large)
python -m src.client — infer against the identity model
gotchas: model_repository version directories MUST be integers (`1`, `2`, ...). Triton silently skips non-integer dirs like `v1` or `latest`.
config.pbtxt `platform` and `backend` are mutually exclusive per model. Pick one — e.g. `backend: "onnxruntime"` for ONNX, `platform: "tensorrt_plan"` for TRT plans.
Input tensor dims use `-1` for dynamic dims, `1` for batch. Getting this wrong returns opaque `inference failed` errors with no stack trace.
The HTTP endpoint is `/v2/` (KServe v2 spec), gRPC is on 8001. Legacy `/api/infer` docs refer to Triton v1 and do not apply.
Ensemble models in config.pbtxt require every sub-model listed in `ensemble_scheduling.step` to already be loaded — load order matters.
TRT engines (`.plan`) are built for a specific GPU + CUDA + TRT version. An engine built on A100 will not run on H100. Rebuild per deploy target.
The nvcr.io registry needs `docker login nvcr.io` for private variants; the public tritonserver image is unauthenticated.
